baseline.note: Re-verified at the v6.8.3 -> v6.8.4 sync (4 upstream commits, merge 6a8b4c724). The SEVEN pre-existing trees are file-count IDENTICAL to the previous baseline (dtrh 1542, fyp 8, goon 184, intake 2138, player 3, tunnel 9, vendor 9), so no disposition changed. ONE TREE GREW: arcademy 88 -> 91 files, all three additions in games/impulse-control/ (casino.js, pressure.js, trickster.js) from the Impulse Control House Rules wave. THE GUARD DID NOT CATCH THE GROWTH AND COULD NOT: fileCountAtBaseline is record data rather than an assertion, and a not-ported tree has no per-tree manifest test to pin it, so a tree the port does not serve can grow by any amount with the suite green. That blind spot is filed as its own board row rather than papered over here. Previous baseline: v6.8.3 / merge fb89d087a (2026-08-22). Guard: client/tests/CcpClient.Tests/UpstreamPayloadInventoryTests.cs. A tree not listed here FAILS the suite; a listed tree that no longer exists upstream FAILS the suite. PIN CLOSED AT SCHEMA 2 (board row "A not-ported upstream payload tree can grow by any amount with the whole suite green"): every entry now carries fileCountAtBaseline + listSha256 and BOTH are asserted, for served and not-ported trees alike, so a tree that CHANGES is a named test failure rather than something a human happened to diff. listSha256 is SHA-256 over the tree's ordinal-sorted, '/'-normalized relative file paths, one per line, UTF-8 - a FILE-LIST digest, not a content digest: it catches an arrival, a removal, a rename and an equal swap, and it deliberately does NOT catch an edit inside an unchanged path, because this repository checks out with core.autocrlf=true and a content hash would differ between a Windows and a Linux checkout of the same commit. pinnedAt + pinReason make a bump carry its reason: the parser rejects a pinReason that does not contain the literal phrase "<fileCountAtBaseline> files" and the literal pinnedAt version, so the count cannot move while the sentence explaining it stays untouched.

trees.boardRow: Port the Arcademy upstream surface, decomposed into its eight slices [P1 OPEN] - SLICES 1 AND 2 LANDED (payload serving + boot handshake; init projection + set-setting echo loop). Slices 3-8 are still open.
trees.note: New at v6.8.3, GREW at v6.8.4 (88 -> 91). Upstream Services/Arcademy/ArcademyHostService.cs and ArcademyMetaStore.cs render Resources/web/arcademy/ (a three.js campus shell: classes, ceremonies, report cards, split-flap board, keybinds, peek, audio). THE TREE IS NOW SERVED but THE SURFACE IS UNREACHABLE, and that is the ported fact rather than an unfinished one: THE DOOR IS SHUT UPSTREAM AS OF v6.8.4 - ArcademyHostService.DoorAvailable is a static readonly false (:116), the Play card ships Visibility=Collapsed (Views/Tabs/PlayTabView.xaml:1312) and is re-asserted from DoorAvailable on every repaint (MainWindow/MainWindow.PlayTab.cs:106-112), and Launch() refuses on the door BEFORE the T2 bar (:136-141). Upstream's stated reason is that Semester 1 landed ahead of its public reveal and 6.8.4 is an auth/stability patch. A HIDE, not a lockband, because a lockband advertises something the account could buy. Porting this surface VISIBLE would therefore ship a feature upstream is deliberately withholding, so the port carries the same single flag, defaulting closed: Features/Arcademy/ArcademyDoor.Available, with ArcademyLaunch.Attend refusing ahead of any allocation (no participant, no bound origin, no window) and ArcademyServingTests pinning that refusal. It also reaches the app-wide remote-media subsystem (FypOnlineCoordinator.For at ArcademyHostService.cs:1513), which is slice 7 and is NOT built: init projects remoteMediaEnabled=false and offlineMode=true, so the page opens no outbound fetch.
